source.title: Spectral Gradient Orthogonalization Improves Differentially Private Training at Scale
source.authors: Sabari Shanmugam; Nick Barnes; Kerry L. Taylor

record.file_problem: Full paper text and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out classification accuracy across batch sizes and optimizer choices in differentially private vision training, extending those comparisons to a DP setting. It does not measure train/test error gaps directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own batch-size and optimizer results. The SNR, recovery-threshold, and Newton–Schulz convergence measurements do not measure the generalization gap or magnitude-aware sharpness, so they are not rows for V7.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out accuracy comparisons across optimizers and batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, testing V4 and V5 in differentially private vision training. Training-error measurements are unnecessary for these versions' held-out-performance components, but their absence prevents assessing whether optimizer differences persist at matched training performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's main paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute spectral processing's benefits to recoverable gradient directions, report harm below a recovery threshold, and find benefits at larger batches and capacities, with complementary temporal filtering. Their numerical summaries need qualification: SVHN's within-DP-Muon batch gain is 7.4 percentage points; 14.9 points is its advantage over SGD at B=4096. The stated 50.3% maximum applies to the WRN-16-4 CIFAR-10 configurations, since WRN-28-10 reaches 56.2%.
record.recipe_differences: Differentially private training with clipped and noised gradients, followed by spectral orthogonalization; compares DP optimizers and batch sizes rather than the original non-private generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with dataset, batch size, privacy budget, architecture, and optimizer. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN have different crossover batch sizes; DP-Muon-S also has a reported decline at B = 4096 on CIFAR-10 and bimodal convergence on SVHN.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient SNR, singular-vector recovery, effective rank, and Newton–Schulz convergence quantify gradient geometry and numerical approximation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral processing can improve private-training accuracy when useful gradient directions survive privacy noise.

record.peer_reviewed: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026; accepted, to appear in Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science
record.problems: The study reports held-out test accuracy rather than training error, so it does not directly measure the train/test gap. Results concern DP training and are not a direct test of the non-private optimizer claims. The stated batch sweeps hold epochs fixed, so the number of gradient steps changes with batch size.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: DP-Adam and DP-Muon values from the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 privacy-budget sweeps (Figures 4, Tables 7–9); optimizer results for full fine-tuning and ImageNet-1k (Table 5 and Table 18); and results for additional models and datasets including WRN-28-10, ResNet-18, Tiny-ImageNet, and temporal-filter combinations (Sections 5.4–5.7, Tables 4, 5, 17, 18). These are held-out accuracy results in additional optimizer, privacy-budget, architecture, or denoising conditions; the batch-sweep rows retained provide the direct evidence for V4 and V5.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold; comparing WRN architectures does not establish post-interpolation width behavior.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.

No language benchmarks, matched training-performance comparison, systematic broader-tuning comparison, or Adam-to-SGD switching. ImageNet includes AdamW, but does not isolate decoupled weight decay as a remedy. Non-private training is not tested.

No language models or longer-training intervention. Learning-rate decay, warmup, and augmentation are used but their ability to remove a batch penalty is not isolated. No matched-step experiment or non-private training comparison.
No magnitude-aware weight sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

missing.what: Within-optimizer DP-Adam batch comparisons: CIFAR-10 39.9, 41.0, 41.8, 42.0, 38.8%; CIFAR-100 25.5, 27.4, 28.9, 26.0, 18.6%; SVHN 29.0, 27.1, 24.4, 22.5, 21.8%, with the tables' uncertainties. Existing Adam rows compare against SGD and do not encode these V5 effects.

DP-Muon-S batch trajectories, including their eventual penalties: CIFAR-10 38.7, 44.0, 44.5, 47.8, 46.3%; CIFAR-100 20.9, 24.8, 26.5, 26.3, 22.6%, with uncertainties. These qualify any claim that spectral recipes uniformly improve with batch size.

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. Every accuracy row should specify that the outcome is best test accuracy selected across epochs, averaged over three seeds, rather than final-epoch accuracy. The standard sweep uses 50 epochs, cosine decay, 5% warmup, clipping, and augmentation; fixed privacy budget also requires changing the noise multiplier with batch size. Consequently, these are DP recipe comparisons, not isolated changes in sampling noise. Overlapping standard deviations do not by themselves establish a null result or statistical significance. Additional optimizer, architecture, fine-tuning, temporal-filter, and privacy-budget results explicitly declared in rows_left_out are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test accuracy.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.

Tests DP-Adam against DP-SGD and DP-Muon on vision tasks, but does not report training performance or language benchmarks; does not test broader tuning, Adam-to-SGD switching, or decoupled weight decay as a remedy.

Tests batch-size effects in DP vision training with fixed epochs. Does not test language models or the cited learning-rate-scaling, warmup, normalization, and regularization adaptations as a systematic set.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based gap measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or measure the effect of such removals on test accuracy.
